comments.body:
## HANDOFF-DF3A: a `/rebar-debug` subagent is root-causing this; do NOT force-close b586 to get around it

State at handoff: reproduced twice, deterministic, fail-closed. A subagent is running the `/rebar-debug`
two-phase protocol against it. No fix attempted yet.

**The one instruction that matters:** the only override this failure offers is `--force-close`, and using
it is the wrong move. A force-closed ticket is the unattested state epic
[rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] spent its whole cycle removing — it is literally why `b586`, `0059` and
`2bc7` were reopened. b586 is therefore left `in_progress` with everything else in place: all acceptance
criteria checked, a fresh PASS plan-review attestation, and `child_closure_findings` reporting 0 blocking
/ 0 uncertified. It is one well-formed verdict away from closing.

**Isolate before concluding.** The leading hypothesis is that re-parenting b586's two orphaned children
(one of which `depends_on` the other) introduced dep/link records into the verifier's assembled context,
and the structured-output step now returns one of those records instead of a verdict. The id in the bad
payload is exactly that link's target. That is a strong correlation and NOT an isolated cause — ordinary
model formatting drift on a large context is a live alternative. The first acceptance criterion is to
reproduce with and without the `depends_on` link present.

**Do not "fix" this by loosening the schema** to accept a link record. If the cause is context assembly
leaking link records into the verdict slot, fix it at the source. Widening `CompletionVerdict` would make
the gate accept garbage, which is worse than the current loud refusal — the fail-closed handling here is
correct, the returned SHAPE is the defect.

If the root cause turns out to be the re-parenting, note that reverting it is not a clean escape: it
would re-orphan two closed, certified tickets and re-break b586's acceptance criteria, which asserted the
parentage. The structure is right; the verifier needs to cope with it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## ROOT CAUSE (Phase 1 complete, confirmed): the verdict scan is schema-blind, not the context assembly

A `/rebar-debug` subagent completed Phase 1. **Root cause proven, and the leading hypothesis in
HANDOFF-DF3A is confirmed as the TRIGGER but refuted as the CAUSE.**

### The defect

The completion verifier's verdict is recovered by scanning the model's free text for JSON, and that
scan selects the first **parseable** JSON object rather than the first that **satisfies the target
schema**. When the verifier quotes a rebar `Dep` record in its prose *before* its verdict, that record
is taken as the structured output and rejected — while a valid `CompletionVerdict` sits later in the
same reply.

Chain, with citations:

1. `llm/capabilities.py:274-276` forces `native_structured_output: False` for all Claude models, so the
   verifier always takes the prompted free-text branch — `llm/structured_run.py:201` builds `Agent(...)`
   with **no `output_type`**. The verdict exists only as text; nothing provider-side enforces the schema.
2. `llm/structured_run.py:213` -> `structured.parse_structured(str(result.output), model_cls)`.
3. Selection is schema-blind in two places in `llm/structured.py`: `:138-140` `_FENCE_RE.search` takes
   the **first** ```json fence in the reply; `:82-118`/`:146-150` `_first_json_object` returns the
   **first balanced object that parses**, in document order (first-wins by design, from bug 67ee).
   Neither consults `model_cls`. The `schema` argument reaches only json-repair (`:169-174`), the last
   resort, never reached here.
4. `llm/structured.py:206-209` raises; the bounded reask (`OUTPUT_RETRIES = 2`) re-pays the call and
   re-raises as `step 'decide@then/verify' failed`.
5. **Provenance of the bad payload is the `show_ticket` TOOL RESULT, not context assembly:**
   `llm/pai_tools.py:219-232` returns the ticket as raw JSON including `deps`, whose shape is
   `types.Dep` (`types.py:52-57`: `target_id`, `relation`, `link_uuid`) — exactly the reported payload.

### Evidence

* **Runtime capture** (one live run, monkeypatch on `parse_structured`): the verifier's actual reply for
  b586 contains, in prose before the verdict,
  ``- S2's deps include `{"relation": "depends_on", "target_id": "f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31"}` ✓`` and then a
  fenced, **complete and valid** `CompletionVerdict` (PASS, 5 criteria). The key order — `relation`
  first, target id last — matches pydantic's middle-truncated render in the original report exactly.
* **Byte-for-byte reproduction**: a `Dep` record + a valid verdict through the real `parse_structured`
  reproduces the reported error verbatim, including pydantic's truncation.
* **Discriminating variants on the real captured reply** (nothing else changed): as emitted -> parses OK;
  dep record in a ```json fence instead of single backticks -> **fails verbatim**; verdict emitted
  unfenced, which the prompt directive at `structured.py:76-79` literally instructs ("no prose, no
  markdown fence") -> **fails verbatim**. The model produced a valid verdict in every case; only the
  *selection* differed.

### What this corrects in this ticket's own premises

* **Trigger confirmed:** the dep record appears only because re-parenting gave b586 children with a
  `depends_on` link, and AC2 requires verifying that link — so the verifier calls `show_ticket`, reads
  the JSON dep, and quotes it. It will recur on any parent whose children depend on each other.
* **Cause refuted:** the links corrupt nothing. Reverting the re-parenting would fix nothing (and would
  re-orphan two certified tickets).
* **"Model formatting drift" refuted** — the model emitted a complete, schema-valid verdict.
* **AC4's premise is refuted and needs re-scoping:** context assembly does **not** leak link records.
  `llm/operations.py:58-61` renders deps as markdown (`- deps: depends_on->f2f3...`), never JSON. There
  is nothing to fix at the assembly source; the JSON arrives via the tool result.
* **Why it is intermittent:** the failure needs both a dep-quoting reply *and* an unlucky layout.

### Fix shape (Phase 2 NOT entered)

Schema-*conditional* refinement in `tolerant_parse`: prefer the first candidate that validates against
`model_cls`; fall back to today's first-wins. ~15 lines, one site, one call site
(`structured_run.py:213`). **This preserves every existing caller**, and the constraint is pinned:
`tests/unit/test_structured.py:47-52` pins first-wins for two verdict objects but calls `tolerant_parse`
**with no schema**, so a schema-conditional change is behaviour-identical there.
`test_structured.py:126-158` encodes the neighbouring contract (recover a verdict past a preceding
non-JSON brace) — the variants above are that same contract violated by a preceding *parseable* object.

Per HANDOFF-DF3A this is still NOT to be fixed by loosening `CompletionVerdict`. The fail-closed refusal
is correct; the selection is the defect. Note the blast radius: `structured.py` is the shared parser
every LLM gate (plan-review, code-review, completion) depends on, so the repair needs the fix plan in
this description, a declared `file_impact`, and a `review-plan` attestation before it is written.

### Prior art — this is the THIRD recurrence of this selection defect

Cited in-code at `structured.py:88-93` and `:186-200`: 67ee/messianic-wild-dassie, artsy-chain-hold,
dash-lure-slag, slit-rubble-braid — the last described as blocking a completion-verifier close
fail-closed. Same function, same class of bug.

### Consequence for b586: it is CLOSED, honestly

The authorized reproduction run drew the lucky formatting and **passed**.
[rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260] is now `closed` with a `completion-verifier` signature present — verified
independently by me (`status: closed`, `signature: completion-verifier`). No `--force-close` was used.
That is the certified close this epic held out for.

*Not determined:* the exact byte layout of the two originally-failing replies (not captured). The
variants show both plausible layouts produce the error verbatim from the real reply, but the specific
one is inferred, not observed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## What a PERMANENT fix looks like — and why the obvious one is unavailable

Design reasoning for the repair, recorded before any code is written. The ~15-line schema-conditional
patch in the RCA above is a mitigation at the selection layer; this is the analysis of what would end
the class. Grounded in the module contracts, not from memory.

### Ruled out: "stop parsing prose, let the provider enforce the schema"

The obvious permanent fix — flip Claude to `NativeOutput` so the schema is enforced provider-side and
there is nothing to scan — is **blocked by a live API constraint, not by inertia**:

* `structured.py:11-15` — PromptedOutput "is also the mode used whenever extended thinking is on,
  because Anthropic currently 400s when extended thinking is combined with a native/forced output
  constraint (*'Thinking may not be enabled when tool_choice forces tool use'*) — a live API
  constraint on the current pydantic_ai output modes, not a relic".
* `output_mode`'s docstring (`:49-55`) — PromptedOutput is chosen precisely because it "stays
  compatible with Claude extended thinking, which pydantic_ai's default ToolOutput mode is not".
* `capabilities.py:262-276` — the `_is_claude -> native_structured_output: False` override is a
  DELIBERATE, documented choice with an explicitly REJECTED alternative recorded
  (`supports_json_schema_output and not supports_thinking`, rejected because it breaks gemini and
  groq). It is a signed S2 contract.

So any permanent fix must live INSIDE the prompted path. Proposals that amount to "just use native
structured output" should be closed as unavailable, citing the above, rather than re-litigated.

Also still ruled out (from HANDOFF-DF3A, and I agree): widening `CompletionVerdict`. The fail-closed
refusal is the one component that behaved correctly here.

### The reframe: this is an architecture, not a parsing bug

A **typed** payload is being recovered from an **untyped** channel by POSITIONAL heuristics. Every fix
so far has refined the heuristic rather than removed the ambiguity, which is why the same function has
now failed five times (67ee/messianic-wild-dassie at `structured.py:88-93`; artsy-chain-hold /
dash-lure-slag / slit-rubble-braid at `:186-200`; this ticket). 67ee's fix was itself "advance to the
next `{` when a candidate does not parse" — a selection refinement that fixed a completion-verifier
fail-closed. A fifth refinement has no reason to converge where four did not.

**The sharpest evidence that the PROTOCOL is at fault, not the model:** `schema_directive`
(`:76-79`) instructs "no prose, no markdown fence" — and the RCA's variant table shows that had the
model OBEYED and emitted the verdict unfenced, the failure would be MORE likely, because then the
`Dep` record quoted in prose is the first parseable object. The current protocol punishes compliance.
That is not model misbehaviour; that is an underspecified channel.

### The four parts of a permanent fix

**1. An unambiguous payload channel.** The primary extractor must key on a delimiter prose cannot
plausibly emit — a sentinel (`<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>> … <<<END>>>`) rather than ```` ```json ````, which is
exactly the delimiter legitimate prose uses to quote a ticket record. Better still, stop hand-rolling
extraction: `structured_run.py:196-201` builds `Agent(model, **kwargs)` with `output_type` defaulting
to `str`, and its own comment names the alternative — "NativeOutput / **PromptedOutput-as-output_type**
inject this automatically". `PromptedOutput(model_cls)` as `output_type` is thinking-compatible AND
schema-aware, and adopting it DELETES rebar-owned parsing surface instead of adding a rule to it.
The reason rebar hand-rolls today is real (json-repair recovers near-misses `PromptedOutput` would
reject), so `tolerant_parse` stays — demoted to a fallback for *validation* near-misses rather than
serving as the primary *locator*. That demotion is the actual fix: locating and repairing are two jobs
and only the second one needs to be tolerant.

**2. Schema-aware selection** — the RCA's ~15 lines. Necessary regardless as defense for the fallback
path, cheap, and caller-safe (`tests/unit/test_structured.py:47-52` pins first-wins but calls
`tolerant_parse` with NO schema, so it is untouched). **Not sufficient alone:** it still loses on a
reply containing two schema-VALID objects, e.g. a draft followed by a correction — which is precisely
the case `_first_json_object`'s docstring says first-wins was designed to make deterministic.

**3. Tests that encode the INVARIANT, not the instance.** This is where I would put the most weight,
because it is what would have caught all five occurrences: a property test asserting that for any
prose `T` and any payload `P` valid under schema `S`, extraction recovers `P` from `T + render(P)` —
plus a corpus of REAL captured replies, starting with the one captured in the RCA above. Each of the
four prior fixes shipped one regression test pinning one layout; the class survived because instances
were pinned and the invariant never was. `test_structured.py:126-158` already encodes the neighbouring
contract (recover a verdict past a preceding non-JSON brace); the invariant is its generalisation.

**4. Evidence that survives the failure.** Diagnosing this needed a monkeypatch and a live billable
re-run, and the two originally-failing replies are unrecoverable — so their exact layout remains
INFERRED, not observed. That is the same evidence-destruction pattern as 4b9e's probe, which this epic
has already paid for once. On parse failure, persist the raw reply (redacted) as an artifact so the
next occurrence is diagnosable without re-running the gate and hoping to lose the formatting lottery.

### Explicitly rejected: reduce the trigger instead of fixing the defect

Making `show_ticket` return rendered markdown instead of raw JSON (`pai_tools.py:219-232`, the
provenance of the offending payload) would cut the trigger rate. **I recommend against it.** Raw JSON
is what lets a verifier check exact field values; blinding the verifier to reduce the odds of
confusing its own parser trades correctness for parser convenience, and treats the symptom at the
wrong end. Worth recording as considered-and-declined so it is not re-proposed as a cheap win.

### Sequencing, and why this is the highest-value item in the open set

(2) is a same-day change and unblocks this failure's shape. (1) and (3) together are what make it
permanent, and should be ONE change, because the property test is what proves the new channel actually
removed the ambiguity rather than relocating it. (4) is independent and small.

`structured.py` is the shared parser behind EVERY LLM gate — plan-review, code-review, completion — so
the blast radius is repo-wide. Concretely that means: this fix plan belongs in this ticket's
DESCRIPTION with a declared `file_impact` and a `review-plan` attestation before any code is written,
and df3a must be CLAIMED first (it is currently `open`). And it is the highest-value open item because
it is a reliability defect in the mechanism that gates every close — b586 closed at all only because
one run drew a lucky layout, which is not a property anyone should be relying on.

### Live corroboration from this same session

Two independent data points arrived while this was being written, both consistent with "the gates'
records are less durable than assumed":

* `rebar review-plan 3b5f --status` returns `verdict: unsigned`, `verified_at_sha: null` — a plan
  review that DID run last session left no attestation, which is [rebar:ab54-…]/[rebar:7084-…]'s
  lost-sidecar-on-lock-contention signature.
* `review-plan` emitted warnings for two ticket directories with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event
  (`358d-8fce-9b96-470a`, `7650-5049-2d90-4da3`), self-described as "debris of an interrupted write".

Neither is df3a's defect, and neither is being folded into it. They are recorded here because they
bear on the same question — how much of a gate's output actually survives — and because they are
measurements, not inferences.

## DESIGN INVESTIGATION (pre-claim): regression theory refuted; fix architecture converged; live derisking experiments in flight

### Regression claim tested and REFUTED
Hypothesis raised in review: this is a regression from the LLM provider-seam epic (f184 07-29 / 2932 07-30). Git archaeology refutes it: the schema-blind selection dates to b82d23f6 (06-21); all four prior instance-fixes landed 07-05..07-07, three weeks BEFORE the seam epic; pre-epic output_mode() already excluded Anthropic from native output (allowlist {openai, google-gla, google-vertex, groq}), so Claude took the identical prompted path under both seams. The seam epic is behavior-preserving for Claude BY DESIGN. What the migration DID change is trigger rate, not the defect: 2932 (07-30) swapped the verifier onto bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 (different formatting distribution), and b586's re-parenting created the first dep-quoting occasion. The July "mitigated period" was instance-pins holding + low exposure, not a closed class.

### OSS prior art (researched with citations, agents' full reports in session artifacts
- pydantic_ai PromptedOutput extraction is SCHEMA-BLIND FIRST-FENCE (strip_markdown_fences) — same defect class; adopting it as output_type is REJECTED on four verified grounds (same defect relocated; breaks the pinned one-call-repair contract — no pre-validation heal hook; loses per-attempt truncation/refusal fast-fail; injects schema as static instruction, reordering our cache prefix split).
- instructor (+deepeval/ragas/guardrails-ai/promptfoo) switched to LAST-valid-object as a prompt-injection security fix: quoted material precedes the model's authoritative answer.
- BAML SAP is the only schema-aware selector, but its equal-score tiebreak is FIRST-in-text-order — it degenerates on exactly our failure shape (two schema-valid candidates); its graded coercion (DefaultFromNoValue penalty-100 still returns a filled object) is a false-accept risk unacceptable for a gate.
- Why nobody combines schema-filter + position: never proposed anywhere (not tried-and-failed); maintainers bet on provider-native output; Pydantic binary validation makes scoring costly. Novelty interrogated and explained.

### Provider matrix finding — structured.py's premise is STALE
The historic Anthropic 400 was tool_choice-x-thinking, NOT structured-output-x-thinking. Anthropic output_config.format (grammar-constrained JSON) is explicitly thinking-compatible; pydantic_ai 1.107.1 auto-promotes to native when thinking is on and the profile supports json_schema output. bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 has a GA NativeOutput path on Converse (also haiku-4-5; opus-4-7/4-8 are EXCLUDED from Converse structured output — the prompted path stays load-bearing for them permanently). Only rebar's _REBAR_OVERRIDES (_is_claude -> native_structured_output False) and output_mode()'s thinking-forces-prompted guard block it. Revisiting that override is a signed-contract change requiring live measurement — experiment E1 below.

### Converged fix architecture (all layers IN SCOPE for this epic, per operator decision)
1. LAYER 1 — provider-native where measured: live-prove NativeOutput+thinking on Bedrock sonnet-4-6/haiku-4-5, then narrow _REBAR_OVERRIDES per measured cell (exact-id override table is the established mechanism) and fix output_mode()'s stale thinking guard. Keep validator bounds client-side (grammar strips min/max on Bedrock).
2. LAYER 2 — prompted-path hardening (permanent for Bedrock opus + fallback everywhere): (a) sentinel channel in schema_directive (<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>...<<<END>>>, LAST block wins), tried before today's pipeline; (b) schema-filtered selection in parse_structured (NOT tolerant_parse — its schema param already means json-repair guidance): enumerate all top-level non-overlapping objects (cap 32) + fenced blocks, key-overlap screen against model_cls.model_fields (required: all-defaults schemas like OverlapVerdict validate {}), full validate_to per candidate, LAST-valid-wins (position-authority principle, consistent with sentinel layer), warn when >=2 validate and last!=first; on no winner fall back to today's pipeline with improved error attribution (last key-screened candidate's validation error).
3. LAYER 3 — invariant tests: property test (any prose incl. schema-valid decoys + payload rendered last -> payload recovered) + captured-reply corpus + pinned adversarial case; trailing-recap hijack documented as the accepted residual. Opt-in raw-reply artifact on parse failure (respecting usage_log's no-prompt/response-in-durable-records posture).

Accepted residuals (explicit): trailing-recap layout loses under last-wins (zero of five recurrences show it; observable via the ambiguity warning); schema-less tolerant_parse stays first-parseable per its determinism pin (divergence documented).

### Experiments in flight (operator-authorized, sonnet/haiku tiers, Bedrock)
- E1 live: NativeOutput x thinking matrix on Bedrock sonnet-4-6/haiku-4-5 incl. the agentic-tools+thinking+native cell (the verifier's real shape) and a bounds-stripping probe.
- E2 live: sentinel directive compliance, n~26, adversarial df3a-shaped prompt with dep record + early schema-valid decoy; measures current-pipeline failure rate vs sentinel vs schema-filtered-last-valid.
- E3/E4 deterministic: selection prototype vs every pinned test in tests/unit/test_structured.py + property trials + df3a byte-shape reproduction; and whether _repair's schema= (Pydantic CLASS passed to json_repair) actually engages or silently falls back.

Results will be posted here; then the description gets the full plan (with file_impact) -> review-plan -> claim -> implement.
EOF
)

## EXPERIMENT RESULTS (E1/E2/E3/E4) — solution VIABLE; four problems identified early

Operator-authorized live+deterministic derisking complete (39 real Bedrock calls total, sonnet-4-6/haiku-4-5 tiers; raw logs+replies in session artifacts exp-e1/e2/e3 dirs).

### E1 — NativeOutput x thinking on Bedrock: PARTIALLY PROVEN
- PROVEN on the wire: outputConfig.textFormat json_schema + thinking works — sonnet-4-6 adaptive (settings thinking=True maps to type=adaptive), haiku-4-5 extended (budget_tokens=2048). No 400; the historic forced-tool_choice error does NOT occur with json_schema output; pydantic_ai auto mode selects native under thinking.
- Bounds ge/le are STRIPPED into descriptions (model emitted 1.0 out-of-bounds) — client-side validators remain mandatory on the native path.
- CRITICAL SCOPE FINDING: tools + thinking + native is wire-legal but the model SKIPPED the required tool 2/2 (one 306s hang); same cell with PromptedOutput called the tool with thinking intact. Layer 1 therefore applies to SINGLE-SHOT (no-tools) structured steps only; the agentic completion verifier STAYS prompted — Layer 2 is the df3a fix, not a fallback.
- PREREQUISITE: pinned botocore 1.40.61 rejects outputConfig client-side (ParamValidationError); needs >=1.43.x.
- Haiku needs the dated profile id us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 (bare alias 400s at request validation).

### E2 — sentinel channel, adversarial df3a shape (n=26): STRONG PASS with 2 catches
- Sentinel compliance 16/16 (exactly one marker pair, valid JSON, true verdict every time); schema-filtered last-valid 26/26; decoy injection 0/26 (sonnet even flagged the decoy).
- CATCH 1 (confound): the sentinel directive licenses analysis prose (quote-in-prose 0% -> 100%), which breaks today's parser 10/10 — directive and extraction MUST ship atomically, with fallback for markerless replies. The control cells' clean runs only show the current "no prose" directive suppressed the trigger at this n, not that today's pipeline is safe (df3a proved it is not).
- CATCH 2 (new hazard): models fence-wrap the quoted dep record, and tolerant_parse's FENCE PRIORITY selects it even before the first-object scan — the fenced-quote path needs its own pinned regression test (covered by the design's all-fenced-blocks candidate enumeration).

### E3 — selection prototype: CALLER-SAFETY PROVEN
- 55/55 bespoke suite; df3a reproduced (3/4 layout variants fail today with "verdict Field required") and prototype recovers ALL 4; property test 500/500 (seed 20250804); 0.1 ms median on 100KB/32-candidate replies.
- MECHANICAL PROOF: all 4 real pinned test files pass 110/110 with the prototype injected as parse_structured (+ injection negative-control). Zero pinned tests change; one NEW pin needed: multi-object-WITH-schema -> last-valid-wins + warning.
- Key-overlap screen is LOAD-BEARING: without it OverlapVerdict/TicketDigest/EpicBugScreenVerdict (all-defaults contracts) degenerate to trailing junk / empty-object wins.
- Measured residuals (accepted, not hidden): trailing-recap schema-valid decoy wins under last-wins (warning marks it; zero of five historical recurrences show that layout); candidate cap should keep the LAST 32, not the first.

### E4 — schema-guided json-repair: ENGAGED
json_repair 0.61.4 schema_from_input accepts Pydantic v2 CLASSES (richer than a schema dict — default_factory fills engage); _repair makes exactly one schema-guided call on the happy path; a missing-required-property payload raises and falls back schema-less exactly as _repair designed. The reviewer's suspicion is resolved: no silent no-op.

### Net: all build-critical decisions now evidence-backed
Fix architecture stands as recorded in the previous comment, with these experiment-driven amendments: Layer 1 scoped to no-tools steps + botocore bump prerequisite + dated haiku profile id; Layer 2 ships directive+extraction atomically + pins the fenced-quote hazard; candidate-cap trims keep the last 32. Next: plan into description, review-plan, claim, implement.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## SCOPE STOP: this is not a mechanical wrong-return-type defect — no patch attempted

A `/rebar-debug` pass was dispatched against this ticket **scoped as a mechanical defect** ("the verifier
returns the wrong record type; fix the type/wiring so it returns a `CompletionVerdict`; do not redesign the
completion-verification contract and do not change verification behavior beyond correcting the returned
record"). That scope does not fit the defect. Stopping in Phase 1 without writing code, and recording why.

### Independent replication of the recorded root cause (not a relay of the earlier comment)

Verified every citation in the ROOT CAUSE comment against the working tree at `origin/main` c3fb869ab5, then
reproduced the failure deterministically and locally:

```python
CV = contracts.completion_verdict_response_model()
reply = "...prose... ```json {\"relation\":\"depends_on\",\"target_id\":\"f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31\"} ``` ...
         Final verdict: ```json {\"verdict\":\"PASS\",\"criteria\":[],\"summary\":\"all met\"} ```"
structured.parse_structured(reply, CV)
```

fails with the reported error **verbatim**, including pydantic's middle-truncated render:

```
structured output failed validation: 1 validation error for CompletionVerdict
verdict
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'relation': 'depends_on'...: 'f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31'}, input_type=dict]
```

`structured.tolerant_parse(reply, schema=CV)` returns `{'relation': 'depends_on', 'target_id': 'f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31'}` —
the `Dep`, not the verdict. Control: the identical reply with the quoted dep record removed parses to
`verdict='PASS' findings=[] criteria=[] summary='all met'`. So the model's verdict is present and valid; only
the **selection** is wrong. Confirms the RCA and re-refutes "model formatting drift".

Citations re-verified as accurate on current `main`:
`llm/structured.py:138-140` (`_FENCE_RE.search` — first fence wins), `:82-118` + `:146-150`
(`_first_json_object` — first *parseable* object wins, `model_cls` never consulted),
`:199` (`parse_structured` = `validate_to(model_cls, tolerant_parse(text, schema=model_cls))` — the schema
reaches json-repair only), `llm/capabilities.py:273-275` (`_is_claude -> native_structured_output: False`),
`llm/structured_run.py:201` (`Agent(model, **kwargs)`, `output_type` defaults to `str`) and `:213`,
`llm/pai_tools.py:219-232` (`show_ticket` returns raw ticket JSON incl. `deps`), `types.py:52-57` (`Dep`).

### Why the mechanical scope does not apply

Nothing returns the wrong type. The verifier's wiring is correct and correctly typed: `parse_structured` is
called with `CompletionVerdict` and *does* validate against it. There is no type annotation, no `return`, and
no call site to correct. The defect is a **selection policy** — `tolerant_parse` picks the first JSON object
that *parses* rather than the first that *satisfies* `model_cls` — and that policy is:

* **deliberate and documented**, not an oversight: `_first_json_object`'s docstring states first-wins exists so
  "a model that emits a draft then a correction does not get the last-wins surprise json-repair gives" (bug
  67ee / messianic-wild-dassie);
* **shared by every structured LLM call in rebar** — plan-review, ticket-digest, overlap, epic-bug-screen — so
  changing it changes verification behavior well beyond the completion verifier. This ticket's own E3
  experiment found the key-overlap screen load-bearing precisely because the all-defaults contracts
  (`OverlapVerdict`, `TicketDigest`, `EpicBugScreenVerdict`) validate `{}` and would degenerate to
  trailing-junk/empty-object wins under a naive schema filter;
* **not correctable at the extractor alone** — E2 recorded that the directive at `structured.py:76-79` ("no
  prose, no markdown fence") and the extraction change must ship **atomically**, because a model that *obeys*
  the current directive makes the failure *more* likely.

Any real fix therefore changes a documented contract and verification behavior across callers. That is the
design decision the dispatch scope explicitly excluded, so no code was written and no claim was taken.

### Recommended disposition

The ticket is already past debugging: root cause proven, four derisking experiments (E1-E4, 39 live Bedrock
calls) complete, and a converged multi-layer fix architecture recorded, with the next step noted as "plan into
description". It needs the **plan + decomposition + plan-review** path, not another debug pass. Re-dispatching
this as a mechanical fix will keep hitting this same stop.

Also unchanged: `b586-2fda-8a15-4260` stays `in_progress`; do not `--force-close` it.

# The completion verifier returns a DEPENDENCY-LINK record where a `CompletionVerdict` belongs, blocking the close

## Reproduced deterministically, twice

`rebar transition b586-2fda-8a15-4260 in_progress closed`, exit 1, fail-closed (no verdict, no
signature, close refused — correct behaviour for an unusable verdict):

```
completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict:
  step 'decide@then/verify' failed: structured output failed validation:
  1 validation error for CompletionVerdict
verdict
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'relation': 'depends_on'...: 'f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31'}, input_type=dict]
```

Two consecutive attempts, both failing at the same step, each returning a TICKET-LINK record
from the ticket's own graph in the slot where the verdict schema is expected (attempt 1
carried `link_uuid`, attempt 2 `relation: depends_on`, both naming `f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31`).

## Root cause (isolated; full trail in comments)

The extraction is schema-BLIND: `tolerant_parse` (src/rebar/llm/structured.py:121) returns the
FIRST parseable JSON object — fenced blocks first (`_FENCE_RE`, :40), then the first balanced
object (`_first_json_object`, :82). The verifier's agentic transcript quotes dep-link records
from `show_ticket` tool results, and the model restates one before its verdict; the quoted
record wins. Trigger isolation is DONE (original AC #1): E3 replayed the captured reply
deterministically with and without the quoted dep record — with it, 3 of 4 layout variants
fail today; without it, all parse (experiment-results comment). Fifth recurrence of this
class; instance history in the design-investigation comment.

## Approach

Schema-filtered candidate selection in `parse_structured` (src/rebar/llm/structured.py:212) —
NOT in `tolerant_parse` (:121), whose `schema` parameter already means json-repair guidance
and whose first-object, schema-less contract is pinned
(tests/unit/test_structured.py::test_tolerant_parse_first_object_wins_on_multi_object).

Selection: enumerate candidates — every fenced block (models fence-wrap quoted records;
measured, E2 catch 2), every top-level non-overlapping balanced object (cap: keep the LAST
32), plus the array-unwrap forms `validate_to` (:177) already accepts. Screen each by
key-overlap against `model_cls.model_fields` — mandatory, because all-defaults contracts in
src/rebar/llm/contracts.py (e.g. the models `default_outputs` at :43 iterates) validate `{}`.
The screen's threshold is DEFINED as: a candidate survives iff the set intersection of its
top-level keys with `model_cls.model_fields` is non-empty (>= 1 shared key); for a top-level
array, the probed dict is the array's sole dict element, mirroring `validate_to`'s unwrap. The
threshold is deliberately minimal because the next stage — full Pydantic validation — already
enforces required fields (a one-key `{"summary": ...}` decoy FAILS `CompletionVerdict`, whose
`verdict` is required); the screen exists solely to kill `{}`/zero-overlap junk that
ALL-DEFAULTS contracts would otherwise accept. Worked example: candidates
`{"relation": "depends_on", "target_id": "f2f3"}` (0 shared keys -> screened out) and
`{"verdict": "pass", "criteria": []}` (2 shared keys -> survives, validates, wins). Known
residual, accepted: against an all-defaults contract, a late single-shared-key decoy can
validate and win under last-wins — the same family as the trailing-recap residual below, and
the >=2-validate warning marks every such case.

Validate each survivor via `validate_to`; the LAST valid candidate wins; when >=2 validate and
last != first, log a warning naming both. No valid candidate -> fall back byte-for-byte to
today's pipeline so the error message and retry behavior are unchanged (when a candidate
passed the screen but failed validation, the raised error is that LAST candidate's validation
error — strictly more diagnostic than today's).

Rationale (G6): last-valid-wins recovers all five historical recurrence layouts (payload
rendered last in each; E3), matches instructor's last-wins prompt-injection posture, and
coheres with the sentinel channel's last-block rule landing in the follow-on story. The
one-call-repair pin and `OUTPUT_RETRIES` (:292) reask loop are untouched.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/structured.py — candidate selection in `parse_structured`; `tolerant_parse`
  untouched
- tests/unit/test_structured.py — new pins (corpus replay, last-wins warning, fallback)
- tests/fixtures/ (new corpus file(s)) — the captured b586 verifier reply + 3 layout variants

## Testing

Contract tier (real reply text -> real parser -> validated contract object; per the shared
test-design standard, this crosses every component of the proven mechanism in-process):

- RED-first corpus replay: the captured b586-shape reply in 4 recorded layout variants — 3
  fail on today's parser, all 4 must pass after.
- Property test: generated prose + schema-valid decoys with the payload rendered last parses
  to the contract (seed 20250804, n=500 — the E3 prototype ran 500/500).
- Mutation check: re-introducing first-wins selection turns the corpus test RED.
- Negative controls: the schema-less `tolerant_parse` pin is unchanged; the full existing
  tests/unit/test_structured.py suite passes unmodified (E3 measured 110/110 with the
  prototype injected).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The captured b586-shape reply (quoted dep record before the verdict) parses to a
      `CompletionVerdict` in all 4 recorded layout variants — checked by the new corpus tests
      in tests/unit/test_structured.py.
- [ ] When >=2 candidates validate and last != first, a warning is logged naming both — checked
      by a caplog unit test.
- [ ] A reply with no schema-valid candidate falls back to today's pipeline byte-for-byte
      (same exception type and message) — checked by a pinned fallback test reusing an
      existing failure fixture.
- [ ] All pre-existing tests/unit/test_structured.py pins pass unmodified — checked by running
      that file's suite under `make test`'s runner.
- [ ] The remedy for the original failure is this parser fix, not `--force-close` (original AC
      #5) — checked by the corpus test asserting the verdict validates.
